note: The Direct family's first gauntlet campaign: the stateless Direct V2 AOT accelerator, real ELF, under solana-program-test. NOTE ON THE DIRECTORY NAME: this tier lives at tools/gauntlet/direct/ rather than tools/gauntlet/tier<N>/ because `tier<N>` turned out to be a global namespace with no allocator and three lanes claimed the same numbers within twenty minutes on 2026-08-27; a family name cannot collide. It is a FAST LANE and says so -- TIERS.md's conditions are answered one by one in the evidence document's `fast_lane` block, and the census records the campaign name with every observation. THE ONE THING A READER MUST NOT MISS: this route's semantic refusals COMMIT. The accelerator holds no state, so a rejected fill is a canonical 160-byte Refused acknowledgement published as return data by a SUCCEEDING transaction. Every `Direct AOT admission refuses *` transaction is therefore bound as `executed`, because that is what the chain reports; crediting it to a refusal code would name a code the program never raised. Only the wire and frame adapters raise the program's own taxonomy. Bindings are authored by the GAUNTLET, never by the campaign, so a label change breaks loudly instead of quietly dropping coverage.

bindings.label: Direct AOT admits *
bindings.note: Twelve admitted frames: the canonical fill-or-kill fill, a partial fill under a resting lifecycle, the minimal fill whose floor fee rounds to zero, prices exactly at the seller limit / the buyer limit / the price scale, a buyer holding exactly gross plus fee, a seller holding exactly the filled claims, both edges of the tightest validity window, a fee rate exactly at the denominator, and the last outcome coordinate in the Market. Each publishes a 616-byte Accepted acknowledgement whose bound request digest the producer re-derives from the submitted bytes with an independent SHA-256.

bindings.label: Direct AOT admission refuses *
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and deliberately bound as executed. Twenty-nine exact-shaped frames the Direct admission relation must reject: zero fill, a partial fill against a fill-or-kill intent, a fill above the signed maximum, an unknown lifecycle, an inexact quote division, prices one unit outside each signed limit and above the price scale, a Market that is not open, slots one unit outside each end of the tightest validity window, a maker generation skew, an outcome mismatch and an out-of-Market outcome, two makers on one side, a seller presented as the buy side, a maker filling against itself, two intents signed for different Markets, a seller one claim short, a buyer one unit short of gross plus fee, three saturating balance additions, a zero price scale, three fee-rate disagreements, and two replay-nonce violations. The route COMMITS and publishes a canonical 160-byte Refused acknowledgement; no refusal code is raised and none is claimed.

bindings.label: Direct AOT frame refuses *
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The stateless route's first act is to refuse any invocation carrying an account at all -- there is no signer, no writable state, no rent and no CPI authority at this boundary, and an accepted account would be the first crack in that. Refuses NonStatelessFrame (0xA000).

bindings.label: Direct AOT wire refuses *
bindings.note: HOSTILE. Seven wires the request adapter must reject before any admission runs: an empty instruction, a request one byte short, a request one byte long, a foreign eight-byte magic, a nonzero reserved header span, and two requests whose header declares an internally consistent but non-Direct bank width (one scalar short, one identity short). They are kept distinct rather than collapsed to one case because they exercise different decoder clauses, and a decoder that lost one of them would still pass a single-case test. All seven refuse InvalidRequest (0xA001).
